picks.editorial_note: Texas A&M's entry into DOE's Genesis Mission exemplifies the week's biggest storyline: a national government-industry-academia coalition using AI, supercomputing, and quantum systems to accelerate scientific discovery, with the highest combined financial and partnership scores in the batch.
picks.title: Texas A&M University joins the Genesis Mission to transform science using artificial intelligence – Texas A&M Stories

picks.editorial_note: An $874 million federal commitment under the CHIPS and Science Act to strengthen domestic semiconductor R&D directly shapes the compute supply chain that underpins all AI research, making this the week's most consequential policy and funding story.
picks.title: Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent With 7 Companies for $874 Million to Accelerate Semiconductor R&D for the Compute Supply Chain

picks.editorial_note: RPI's selection for two Genesis Mission Phase I projects, including AI-guided rare-earth materials work with a national lab, carries the highest scientific score among this week's DOE awards and shows deep technical ambition beyond a symbolic partnership.
picks.title: RPI Selected for Two U.S. Department of Energy Genesis Mission Projects

picks.editorial_note: UC Davis's brain-computer interface restoring natural speech to an ALS patient is a genuine scientific milestone with immediate, tangible human impact, distinguishing it from the week's funding and partnership announcements.
picks.title: Giving People Their Voice

picks.editorial_note: Cambridge's role in the CuspAI-led AI Materials Foundry establishes a global industry-academia network for AI-driven materials discovery, reflecting real cross-border commercial-academic integration rather than a single-institution grant.
picks.title: Cambridge researchers contribute to AI Materials Foundry

picks.editorial_note: University of Florida's six-year, $511 million AI investment record is a rare data point showing the sheer institutional scale AI research funding has reached, useful context for the many smaller awards reported this week.
picks.title: AI year in review

picks.editorial_note: A new $21.5 million NSF AI Institute for Human-AI Cooperation, spanning Delaware, Florida, Princeton, and Penn, targets clinician-AI collaboration in rehabilitation—a substantial multi-institution federal investment with clear healthcare applications.
picks.title: UF researchers join new NSF-funded AI institute to transform rehabilitation and health care

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's deployment of the first AI-driven telescope under the Genesis Mission demonstrates a concrete, novel application of AI to scientific instrumentation rather than a funding or planning announcement.
picks.title: First AI-driven telescope goes stargazing

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's Generalist-Specialist Collaboration framework for disease diagnosis is a novel AI architecture with demonstrated accuracy gains in a real clinical use case, representing genuine research innovation rather than institutional news.
picks.title: HKUST Develops Novel AI Framework Enabling Efficient Collaboration between Generalist and Specialist Models for Disease Diagnosis
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: Nebraska's $18 million NSF MRSEC award to build a materials research center around ultra-thin quantum materials is a substantial, multi-year federal investment aimed at more energy-efficient computing hardware.
picks.title: Husker team earns elite NSF award to drive next generation of materials research
